title: Low Country Boil
subtitle: American Southern seafood boil with prawns, sausage, and sweetcorn
excerpt: The great outdoor feast of the South Carolina Lowcountry: prawns, andouille sausage, sweetcorn, and potatoes boiled together in a spiced court bouillon then piled on a table covered in newspaper. A communal dish eaten with the hands.

recipe.sourceNotes: The low country boil (also called Frogmore Stew, named after the small South Carolina community where it is said to have been codified by a National Guardsman named Richard Gay in the 1960s) is the signature communal feast of the South Carolina Lowcountry coastal region. The dish brings together the seafood, corn, and sausage traditions of the coastal South into a single pot. Everything is added in staggered sequence so that each ingredient is cooked correctly: the sausage and corn first, the potatoes next, and the shrimp last since they cook in minutes and turn rubbery if overdone. The boiling liquid is heavily spiced with Old Bay or a similar Chesapeake-style seafood spice blend. The result is drained and tumbled onto a paper-lined table, with drawn butter, hot sauce, and bread for the inevitable mopping.

content.text: Add each ingredient in sequence and allow the liquid to return to the boil between additions. The prawns go in last and cook for no more than 3 minutes; they will continue cooking in the residual heat after draining. Taste the broth partway through and add more spice if needed: it should be well-seasoned enough to flavour everything cooked in it.

items.preparation: fresh corn cobs cut into 4 cm rounds; or 400 g tinned sweetcorn

content.text: Fill a very large pot with 5 litres of water. Add the salt, paprika, cayenne, thyme, bay leaves, peppercorns, garlic, and lemon halves. Bring to the boil. Add the andouille sausage and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and sweetcorn. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the potatoes are just tender when pierced. Taste the broth and adjust the seasoning.

Add the prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until just pink and cooked through. Drain everything immediately. Spread on a large tray or paper-covered table. Drizzle with melted butter and serve with hot sauce, lemon wedges, and bread.
